messages:
Ava: Quick thread — I'm sketching a 'safety gates' UX for automated rollouts and want feedback on which signals we should surface prominently and how operators should act. starting point: latency spike, error-rate bump, quality regressions from eval sets.
Ravi: +1. Do we want a single aggregated health score or separate panes per signal?
Lina: Separate but correlated. ops love a single oatmeter, but for debugging you need the split (latency, 5xx rate, p99, model-confidence drift).
Marta: Also add infra signals: GPU queue depth, OOMs, node restarts. Those often precede app-layer errors.
Theo: From product side: show which rollback action will happen automatically vs which requires manual approval. People get nervous about invisible rollbacks.
Ava: Good point. Proposal: UI shows current rollout step, a list of active safety gates, and an explicit "auto-action" column: fallback to variant X, reduce concurrency, or pause. Also show time-window that triggered it.
Jun: For telemetry links — include quick filters: "show traces for affected requests" (button) and a direct link to the exact query in observability with prefilled time range + tags. Saves so much time.
Lina: Implementation note: we should emit a structured event when a gate fires, e.g. `gate.fire` with fields: gate_id, rule, metric_values, action, rollout_id, commit_sha. That makes audits/querying trivial.
Marta: +1 on structured events. Also include a short human-readable summary in the event so support can triage without a console.
Ravi: UX question: do we expose rule expressions to product folks (e.g., "p99 > 1500ms for 5m") or only show natural language?
Theo: Both. Natural language in main view, expandable to raw rule for power users. Link to the rule editor for quick edits.
Ava: Edge case: two gates fire at once (latency + quality). What action wins? Our current idea: action precedence table + composite policy where we can define if actions are merged or if highest-severity wins. Thoughts?
Lina: Make precedence configurable per rollout. Default: safety-first — choose the most conservative (fallback to lower-capacity model). But sometimes you want to degrade differently (reduce concurrency first).
Jun: Need an audit timeline in the UI: show gate history with thumbnails: when fired, metric delta, auto-action, who (system or manual), and ability to annotate.
Marta: Also capture the snapshot of related traces and a short sample of inputs that triggered the quality regression (scrubbed). That helps model teams reproduce.
Ava: Re permissions: only rollout-owners + SRE can change auto-action defaults; others can view and request override. Add an "escalate" flow in UI to ping oncall.
Ravi: API design: POST /rollouts/:id/gates -> returns gate status. We'll also add webhooks for `gate.fired` and `gate.resolved`. Any objections?
Lina: Webhooks good. Also stream to a kinesis/topic for long-term analytics and build-percentage correlation queries.
ops-bot: ALERT: gpu-node-14 restarted 3x in last 10m — correlates with p50 increase.
Marta: ops-bot note acknowledged — we should show correlated infra alerts inline under the gate event.
Ava: UX mock next steps: I'll sketch a compact header with rollout state + primary action, a stacked list of gates with expanders, and an audit timeline panel. Jun can wire the quick link buttons.
Jun: I can prototype the quick-filter deep links this week. Will use the observability stable URL params.
Theo: Also want an unobtrusive banner for apps consuming the model (webhooks) when a fallback happens so downstream teams are aware.
Ravi: Implementation doc checklist: metric definitions, event schema, webhook spec, UI mock, permissions matrix, and backfill script to tag historical gate events. I'll draft it.
Lina: Small API nit: include `model_variant` and `quantization_profile` in gate events — we fallback by variant a lot.
Ava: Nice. If no one objects I'll create the RFC and attach the mock + event schema. Please add any must-have fields you want in the gate event as comments on the RFC. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Deployment notice: canary rollout service updated at 1954326900 by Ravi — no errors seen in initial checks.
Marta: thanks — I'll keep an eye on infra for the next hour.
Ava: Thanks all. Closing for now — will ping when RFC ready.
